Jemursari 51-57 Surabaya Indonesia. Abstract Indonesia is a country that has various kinds of natural beauty and interesting cultural heritage. The Indonesian government has designated 10 New Bali's, then refined into 5 National Tourism Strategic Areas to create new mainstay destinations, namely Toba, Likupang, Mandalika, Borobudur, and Labuan Bajo. Providing new tourist attractions, followed by amenity infrastructure and accessibility, will drive new demand. In this context, this study will examine the influence of E-WoM, cultural events, destination image, nationalism, and government support variables on intention to visit. This quantitative research was conducted by distributing questionnaires to 200 respondents. The results of the study explain that W-WoM has a significant positive relationship to destination image, cultural events have a significant positive effect on destination image, destination image has a significant positive relationship to visit intentions, nationalism manages to moderate the relationship between destination image and intention to visit, as well as government support variables also managed to moderate the relationship between destination image and intention to visit. By understanding the influence of these variables, this research can provide valuable insights for the government, tourism industry players, and related stakeholders to increase tourist interest and visits to these destinations. This research is expected to provide a deeper understanding of the factors influencing tourist intentions to visit certain destinations. Thus, the results of this research can become the basis for developing more effective marketing and promotion strategies, sustainable destination management, and better government support for the growth of the tourism sector in Indonesia. In this way, there will be an even distribution of tourist visits, not only concentrated in Bali. Keywords: E-WoM, cultural event, destination image, nationalism, government support, intention to visit 1. Introduction Indonesia, rich in natural and cultural wonders, is actively promoting its tourism industry (Pratama & Briliana, 2019). Indonesia is a country that has various kinds of natural beauty and interesting cultural heritage. One of the popular destinations in Indonesia is Labuan Bajo (Cole, 2017; Ayachi & Jaouadi, 2017; Dwipayanti et al., 2022), Lake Toba (Paramitha et al., 2019; Simarmata & Saragih, 2020; Siti Hajar, 2022; Tanjung et al., 2024; Wiweka et al., 2020), Likupang (Saputri et al., 2023; Pratiknjo et al., 2024; Ganda et al., 2021; Suatan, 2020; Ambalao et al., 2022), Borobudur (Fatimah, 2015; Harsono & Wijayanto, 2022; Hapsari, 2021; Kausar, 2010), and Mandalika (Kurniati & Suryanto, 2023; Estriani, 2019; Rahmatika et al., 2017; Lidona Aprilani & Fathurrahman, 2021; Azizurrohman et al., 2023; Fauzi et al., 2022). Each of these destinations has a unique charm and attracts the attention of both local and international tourists. The beauty of Indonesia is, of course, an opportunity for Indonesia to get more money from other countries for our country and revive the regional economy around tourist areas. Data from the Ministry of Tourism and Creative Economy (2023) explains that tourist visits to Indonesia have reached 1.4 billion and are targeted to reach IDR 111.7 trillion in 2023 (www.mpr.go.id). Based on this target, the government should be able to increase tourist visits to destinations in Indonesia. Purwaningwulan & Ramdan (2022) examine how promoting local tourist destinations online in the current era of the pandemic is impacting the economy in Indonesia. Intention to visit is important in tourists' decisions to choose certain destinations (Chi, 2022). Many factors can affect the intention to visit, such as Electronic Word of Mouth (E-WoM), cultural events, destination image, nationalism, government support, and other factors that can increase the intention to visit. Yerizal (2019) explained that E-WoM can affect a picture of a place where you want to go which can later affect the interest of tourists visiting a destination. E-WoM is an opinion, and tourist recommendations, have become a very influential source of information in the tourism industry. Tourists tend to trust reviews and recommendations from other users before visiting a destination (Choirisa, 2021). Positive reviews spread through E-WoM creating a good impression of a place can make people want to visit it. Multidiscip. Rev. Cultural events such as music festivals, art exhibitions, and traditional celebrations can attract tourists by showcasing local cultural heritage and traditions. Experiences gained from cultural events can create strong impressions and influence tourists' intentions to explore these destinations (Wiyana et al., 2018). The picture of where you want to go is important in deciding if you want to visit there. Destination image reflects the perception and image held by tourists about a place. Positive images of natural beauty, cultural uniqueness, tourist attractions, and quality of service can influence tourists' interest and intention to visit these destinations. Suprina et al., (2023) stated, that there is a strong and positive relationship between the perception of a city, the satisfaction of tourists, and their loyalty towards the city. In addition, this study focuses on using a moderating variable, namely nationalism. Nationalism, or pride and national identity, can also affect intentions (Hamrén, 2021). Tinson & Saren (2022) stated personal nationalism involves including others, interacting with them, and individualizing one's experiences. People strengthen their nationalism by connecting with others and representing them, as well as by finding different ways to belong and by relating their experiences to their families. These findings provide a detailed understanding of how tourists at a national heritage site adopt and interpret national symbols, myths, and values through tourism. Bhandari (2022) stated, that using national symbols in tourism is an illustration of commercial nationalism, where the narrative of nationalism is employed to confront factors that weaken the perceived independence of a nation. Stokburger-Sauer (2011) stated, the identification and personality of a nation's brand strongly affect people's intention to visit. Tourists with a high level of nationalism may be more inclined to choose domestic destinations as a form of support for their own country. This can moderate the impact of how people perceive a destination on their intention to visit it. Furthermore, government support has an important role in developing and promoting tourism destinations. Government support in infrastructure development, promotion, policies and regulations, and environmental management can strengthen the image of the destination and influence tourists' intentions. Research regarding government support in tourism has been conducted by earlier scholars, such as regional government planning regulations and policymakers believe that the government must step in to alleviate the market failure in rural tourism development (Aly et al., 2019), government, at all levels, should support tourism businesses (Ramukumba & Ferreira, 2016), government provided support and implemented measures to help many tour guides during the lockdown (Nyawo, 2020), government assistance impacts a company's ability to gain a competitive edge. 2. Conversely, less government support had a lesser impact on the adoption of technological innovation. 2.6. Discussion 4.1. E-WoM → destination image E-Wom has a significant positive influence on Destination Image. The results showed that E-WoM has a significant positive effect on destination image with a p-value of 0.003, meaning that the more positive E-WoM is spread on social media, the better the tourist's perception of a destination, the more positive it will be. E-WoM is a form of online communication in which people share their experiences, opinions, and recommendations about a product, service, or tourist destination with others through digital platforms such as social media, websites, forums, or reviews online. E-WoM has a strong impact on how people perceive a destination. When looking for information about a particular travel destination, they often rely on online reviews, recommendations, or the experiences of others shared online. In the digital era, E-WoM has gained significant influence as a source of information. People tend to trust the reviews and recommendations of other users visiting the destination. If positive reviews and comments are dominant, creating a positive image of the destination is possible and increases people's interest in visiting it. On the other hand, if many negative reviews or bad experiences are shared online, this can damage the destination's image and discourage people from visiting it. Therefore, tourist destinations need to pay attention and respond properly to reviews and comments shared online. This is also backed up by the research of Utama and Giantari (2020), Kusumawati et al., (2019) and Rizky et al., (2017) which explain that E-WoM has a strong positive impact on how a destination is perceived. 4.2. Cultural events → destination image The results showed that cultural events had a significant positive influence on destination image with a p-value of 0.000, this means that if a cultural event is of high quality and enjoyable for tourists, their perception of the destination will be more positive. Cultural events can greatly impact the perception of a place. Cultural events include various events such as music festivals, art exhibitions, traditional celebrations, dance performances, or regional cuisine that reflect the cultural heritage of a place. Cultural events highlight and introduce the distinctive cultural aspects of a place. This can help build the destination's https://www.malque.pub/ojs/index.php/mr Satrya et al. (2026) 6 image as a place rich in culture and unique heritage. Cultural events provide tourists with hands-on experiences, enabling them to get involved in local traditions and culture. This positive and memorable experience can form a positive perception of the destination. If tourists feel fascinated, entertained, or inspired by the cultural events they attend, they are likelier to share their experiences with others through e-WOM or social media. This is of course supported by Xu (2022) which explains that cultural events can shape an image of a destination. 4.3. Destination image → intention to visit The results showed that cultural events greatly impact the perception of a place on the destination image with a p-value of 0.000, meaning that the more positive the e-WOM spread on social media, the perception of a destination by a tourist will be more positive. Destination image refers to the perception and image that is owned by an individual about a particular tourist destination or place. This perception can be formed through various sources of information, including advertisements, social media, traveler reviews, personal experiences, and recommendations from others. Destination image can also influence the perception of the value or benefits that will be obtained from visiting the destination. Suppose the destination image communicates added values such as natural beauty, cultural uniqueness, opportunities to learn, or unforgettable experiences. In that case, tourists will feel that visiting the destination will provide higher value and can influence their intention to visit. Thus, the destination image can be an important factor influencing the intention to visit. Destinations that succeed in building a positive image of their uniqueness, quality, and attractiveness will tend to attract the interest and intention of tourists to visit them. This is also supported by the research by Kanwel et al., (2019) and Prayogo et al., (2017), which explain that destination image significantly influences visit intention. 4.4. Nationalism x destination image → intention to visit The results showed that nationalism can moderate between destination image and visit intention with a p-value of 0.002. Nationalism is a factor that can moderate the impact of how a destination is perceived and influences the likelihood of someone wanting to visit that place. Nationalism refers to individuals' pride and strong national identity for their own country. Individuals who have high levels of nationalism may tend to have a strong preference for visiting tourist destinations within their country. Tourists with a high nationalist spirit will have a sense of attachment to their country or love their own country. Therefore tourists with high nationalism tend to visit domestic destinations as a form of support for their country. Therefore, the higher the nationalist attitude that tourists have, the better the perception of tourists towards destinations in Indonesia which can ultimately affect interest in visiting a destination. 4.5. Government support x destination image → intention to visit The study results show that government support can moderate between destination image and visit intention with a p- value of 0.000. Government support can moderate the impact of how a destination is perceived on the desire to visit or visit that destination. Government support has an important role in developing and promoting tourism in a country or region. Government support in developing tourism infrastructure, such as airports, roads, public transportation, accommodation, and other tourism facilities, can enhance the image of a destination. Good infrastructure affects tourists' perceptions of ease of accessibility and convenience when visiting a place. If the government supports the development of adequate tourism infrastructure, this can strengthen the image of the destination and increase tourist intentions to visit it. With adequate government support, the impact of how a destination is perceived on the desire to visit or actually visit that destination can be strengthened. Government support in infrastructure development, promotion and marketing, environmental management, as well as policy and regulatory facilitation, can give tourists the trust and confidence to visit destinations. 5. Final Considerations The conclusions from this research include: From the results of the study, it can be concluded that: 1. E-WoM has a significant positive effect on destination image. Positive E-WoM spread online can strengthen the destination's image in the eyes of tourists. 2. Cultural events also have a significant positive influence on the destination image. Cultural events that display the cultural heritage of a place can shape positive perceptions about the destination. 3. Destination image has a significant positive effect on the intention to visit. A positive destination image can increase tourist interest and intention to visit the destination. 4. Nationalism can moderate the effect of destination image on the intention to visit. A high level of nationalism can influence tourists' preferences to prefer domestic destinations and local cultural experiences. https://www.malque.pub/ojs/index.php/mr Satrya et al. (2026) 7 5. Government support can also moderate the effect of destination image on the intention to visit. Government support in infrastructure development, promotion, environmental management, and tourism policies can strengthen the influence of a destination's image and motivate tourists to visit it. Thus, E-WoM, cultural events, destination image, nationalism, and government support are interconnected factors that shape tourists' intentions and decisions to visit a destination. JSON: Name: indonesia_super_priority_visit_model Title: Partial least squares structural equation modeling of electronic word-of-mouth, cultural events, destination image, nationalism, and government support on intention to visit Indonesia's five super-priority tourism destinations Short Hypothesis: Positive electronic word-of-mouth and higher-quality cultural events increase destination image, which increases intention to visit the five Indonesian super-priority destinations, and the positive effect of destination image on intention to visit is strengthened by higher nationalism and stronger perceived government support. Related Work: Prior research has examined electronic word-of-mouth (E-WoM), cultural events, destination image, nationalism, and government interventions as factors influencing travel intention. Existing approaches typically use cross-sectional surveys and structural equation modeling (often PLS-SEM) to estimate direct and mediated relationships between E-WoM, events, destination image, and visit intention. Some studies test moderators such as identity or institutional support but most treat moderators and mediators separately and rely on small, convenience samples. Common limitations include reliance on self-reported cross-sectional data (limiting causal inference), underpowered samples for moderation tests, inconsistent measurement scales across studies, limited evaluation of predictive performance, and scarce comparisons between alternative model specifications. Few works evaluate model robustness through ablation or nested-model comparisons, and behavioral outcomes (actual visits) are rarely observed. Geographic concentration and sampling bias reduce generalizability across destinations and international/domestic visitor segments. Abstract: This study addresses the determinants of tourists' intention to visit Indonesia's five government-designated super-priority destinations by quantitatively modeling how electronic word-of-mouth (E-WoM) and cultural events shape destination image and how destination image influences visit intention under the moderating effects of nationalism and government support. We propose to collect structured questionnaire data from visitors to the five destinations and estimate a measurement and structural model using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM). The main contribution is a jointly estimated mediated-moderated model that quantifies direct effects of E-WoM and cultural events on destination image, the mediating role of image on intention to visit, and the moderating impacts of nationalism and perceived government support. Expected outcomes include ranked effect sizes, model predictive metrics, and evidence on whether moderating factors amplify or attenuate image-to-intention links. Results will inform evidence-based prioritization of communication and policy levers for destination management. Experiments: Dataset: primary survey of individuals who have visited or intend to visit one or more of the five Indonesian super-priority destinations (Toba, Likupang, Mandalika, Borobudur, Labuan Bajo); target N = 400 (minimum N = 200 for replication), collected using purposive sampling stratified by destination and visitor origin (domestic/international). Measures: validated multi-item Likert scales (1–5) for E-WoM (5 items), Cultural Events quality/appeal (5 items), Destination Image (4 items cognitive + 4 items affective), Nationalism (4 items), Perceived Government Support (4 items), Intention to Visit (4 items). Baselines: (1) structural model without mediators (direct effects only); (2) mediation-only model (image mediates E-WoM and events → intention); (3) moderation-only model (direct effects moderated); (4) covariance-based SEM (CB-SEM) re-estimation. Evaluation metrics: measurement model: indicator loadings, AVE, composite reliability, Cronbach's alpha, HTMT; structural model: path coefficients, bootstrapped p-values, R^2 for endogenous constructs, effect sizes f^2, predictive relevance Q^2 (blindfolding), SRMR for model fit; comparative metrics: change in R^2 and path coefficients across ablations. Experimental setup: 1) Preprocess: remove responses with >20% missing, impute remaining with item median, test normality and multicollinearity (VIF). 2) Run PLS-SEM in SmartPLS or equivalent with bootstrap = 5000 subsamples for significance. 3) Test measurement model validity and reliability then assess structural paths. 4) Test mediation via bootstrapped indirect effects. 5) Test moderation by creating interaction terms (product indicator approach) and report interaction path coefficients and simple slopes (low/mean/high moderator). 6) Ablation study: remove E-WoM, remove Cultural Events, remove moderators sequentially and record ΔR^2 and ΔQ^2. 7) Multi-group analysis: domestic vs international visitors and by destination; report path heterogeneity and invariance tests. 8) Sensitivity: repeat analysis with N=200 and N=400 subsamples to assess power and stability. Reproducibility: publish code, synthetic data schema, and model specification. Risk Factors and Limitations: Self-report measures and cross-sectional design limit causal inference; intention-to-visit is a proxy and may not predict actual visitation behavior. Purposive or convenience sampling and limited international respondent access produce sampling bias and limit generalizability. Moderation tests require larger samples; underpowered moderation analyses may produce unstable estimates. Common method variance may inflate relationships. Measurement invariance across cultural groups or languages may fail, compromising comparisons. Multicollinearity between predictors (E-WoM, cultural events, image components) can bias path coefficients. Model misspecification (omitted confounders such as price or health risk perceptions) can lead to biased estimates. Reliance on PLS-SEM assumptions and algorithmic settings may affect results; different estimation methods (CB-SEM) can produce divergent inferences. External shocks (pandemic, travel restrictions, policy changes) can alter visitor intentions and reduce temporal validity.
